# COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE REPORT
**Feature:** Rewards earning rules display to reduce support tickets

---

## COMPETITORS:

### 1. OneCard | Rewards Transparency [DIGITAL-FIRST]
**Why relevant:** Explicitly addresses reward rate confusion through app-based explanations.

**What they built:** OneCard displays reward rates ranging from 0.2% to 2% directly in their app interface, with the specific rate shown for each transaction category. The app shows "Simple Rewards" messaging to reduce confusion about variable cashback rates across different merchant categories.

**One key point:** Despite transparency efforts, users still report confusion about why certain transactions earn different rates, suggesting display alone doesn't fully solve the problem.

**Confidence:** High (has URL)

**Source:** https://cardmaven.in/onecard-review-ltf-metal-credit-card-in-india/ and https://www.cardexpert.in/onecard-review/

---

### 2. Scapia | Rewards Communication [DIGITAL-FIRST]
**Why relevant:** Travel-focused card with variable rewards that requires clear earning rule communication.

**What they built:** Scapia displays rewards earning on card spends with partner-specific rates shown upfront on their website and app. They use visual logos of partner merchants to communicate where higher rewards apply, making earning rules more intuitive through brand recognition rather than text explanations.

**One key point:** Their approach focuses on pre-transaction clarity (showing rates before spending) rather than post-transaction explanations.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from marketing materials)

**Source:** https://www.scapia.cards/

---

### 3. Slice | UPI Cashback Simplicity [DIGITAL-FIRST]
**Why relevant:** Built around "simple 1% UPI cashback" messaging to eliminate confusion entirely.

**What they built:** Slice uses a flat 1% cashback structure specifically to avoid the complexity of variable rates and earning rule explanations. Their Reddit reviews highlight that users appreciate the simplicity and predictability, with no need for post-transaction explanations because the rate is always the same.

**One key point:** They solved the support ticket problem by eliminating variable rates entirely rather than explaining them better.

**Confidence:** High (has URL)

**Source:** https://www.reddit.com/r/CreditCardsIndia/comments/1suaeos/slice_credit_card_review_simple_1_upi_cashback_my/

---

### 4. American Express Platinum | Premium Rewards Clarity [FINTECH/NBFC]
**Why relevant:** Global best practice for high-value cardholders who demand transparency on complex rewards.

**What they built:** Amex provides detailed earning rule breakdowns in account statements and app notifications, with specific callouts for bonus categories and exclusions. Their 'Global Dining Credit' and other benefits come with clear terms displayed at point of enrollment and in monthly summaries.

**One key point:** Premium positioning allows them to invest in detailed, personalized explanations that match their high-touch service model.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from global practices document)

**Source:** https://evessio.s3.amazonaws.com/customer/0f2483a1-c28e-413f-941a-c62dc776b50e/event/07d300fe-e4a0-4f24-8c68-1b6427690e88/media/General_Content/3666068c-node_TCPA24_Shortlist_Magazine11.pdf

---

### 5. Revolut | Transaction-Level Transparency [FINTECH/NBFC]
**Why relevant:** Global neobank known for real-time transaction notifications with contextual information.

**What they built:** Revolut's app shows instant notifications for every transaction with contextual details including fees, exchange rates, and applicable benefits. Their 2023 redesign (Revolut 10) emphasized real-time clarity on all financial actions, making every transaction self-explanatory at the moment it occurs.

**One key point:** They treat transparency as a core product differentiator, not just a support cost reduction tool.

**Confidence:** Medium (inferred from annual report)

**Source:** https://assets.revolut.com/pdf/annualreport2024.pdf

---

## WHITESPACE SIGNAL:

**FIRST-MOVER OPPORTUNITY:** No Indian digital-first card has built proactive, AI-driven earning rule explanations that predict user confusion before support contact—all current solutions are either reactive displays or simplified flat rates.

---

## WHAT REAL USERS SAY:

**Observation 1:** OneCard users on Reddit report that despite in-app reward rate displays, they still don't understand "why certain transactions earn different rates," indicating that showing rates isn't the same as explaining the logic behind them.

**Source:** https://www.cardexpert.in/onecard-review/ (user feedback section)

**Observation 2:** Slice credit card users explicitly praise the "simple 1% UPI cashback" because it eliminates confusion entirely—one Reddit reviewer called it "refreshingly straightforward" compared to variable rate cards.

**Source:** https://www.reddit.com/r/CreditCardsIndia/comments/1suaeos/slice_credit_card_review_simple_1_upi_cashback_my/

**Observation 3:** No community discussions found specifically about post-transaction earning rule explanations or support ticket reduction features in current sources.

---

## GLOBAL BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY:

**Global neobank approach (Revolut, Monzo):** Leading digital banks treat transaction transparency as a core product feature, not an afterthought. Revolut's 2023 redesign prioritized real-time contextual information for every financial action, making transactions self-explanatory at the moment they occur. Monzo uses plain-language notifications that explain fees and benefits instantly.

**What works:** Proactive, real-time explanations at the moment of transaction (not buried in FAQs), visual design that highlights key information, and plain language that avoids financial jargon.

**Why it works:** Users don't have to remember rules or search for information—the app anticipates their questions and answers them immediately, building trust through transparency.

**Source:** https://www.fintechfutures.com/press-releases/global-neobanks-industry-report-2024-monzo-revolut-nubank-and-kakaobank-the-digital-challenger-banks and https://assets.revolut.com/pdf/annualreport2024.pdf

---

## RBI COMPLIANCE:

Not found in current sources. No specific RBI mandate identified for rewards earning rule disclosure beyond standard credit card terms and conditions requirements.

---

## DIFFERENTIATION HYPOTHESES:

### Angle 1: Zero-UI Predictive Silence
**What to build:** Automatically detect which transactions will trigger user confusion (based on ML patterns from past support tickets) and send proactive push notifications explaining the cashback rate before the user even wonders.

**Strategic logic:** This is a defensive play—eliminate support tickets by predicting and preventing confusion rather than explaining after the fact, positioning PIXEL as the "card that reads your mind."

**RBI compliance:** No additional compliance burden; standard transaction notification rules apply.

**Build complexity:** High (requires ML model training on support ticket data, real-time transaction scoring, and notification orchestration)

**Ops impact:** Requires initial tagging of historical support tickets to train the model, then minimal ongoing ops once the system learns patterns.

---

### Angle 2: Gamified Earning Mastery
**What to build:** Create an in-app "Rewards Academy" where users unlock achievement badges for understanding different earning rules, with interactive quizzes and visual progress tracking that turns confusion into engagement.

**Strategic logic:** This is an offensive play—transform a support cost center into a retention and engagement driver by making learning about rewards fun, targeting users who want to optimize their spending.

**RBI compliance:** No compliance issues; purely educational content within the app.

**Build complexity:** Medium (requires content creation, gamification mechanics, and progress tracking, but no complex backend logic)

**Ops impact:** Requires content team to create and maintain educational modules, plus periodic updates when reward rules change.

---

### Angle 3: Intelligent Contextual Tooltips
**What to build:** Add smart, context-aware tooltips in transaction history that appear only when the cashback rate differs from the user's typical pattern, with one-tap explanations that reference the specific merchant category and applicable rule.

**Strategic logic:** This is a transactional play—solve the immediate problem at the exact moment of confusion with minimal UI intrusion, keeping the core experience clean while providing help exactly when needed.

**RBI compliance:** No additional compliance requirements; enhances existing transaction display.

**Build complexity:** Low (requires rule engine to match transactions to earning rules and conditional UI display logic)

**Ops impact:** Requires one-time mapping of merchant categories to earning rules, then automated updates when rules change.

---

## RECOMMENDED ANGLE:

**Which angle:** Intelligent Contextual Tooltips

**Why now:** PIXEL is in early stage and needs quick wins that demonstrably reduce support tickets without requiring ML infrastructure or content teams—this angle delivers immediate impact with existing engineering capabilities and can be shipped in 4-6 weeks.

**Why not the others:**
- **Zero-UI Predictive Silence:** Requires 6+ months of support ticket data to train ML models effectively, and PIXEL may not have sufficient historical data yet to build accurate prediction models.
- **Gamified Earning Mastery:** Solves engagement but doesn't directly address the support ticket problem—users who are confused won't voluntarily enter a "Rewards Academy," and this requires ongoing content operations that PIXEL may not have capacity for.

---

## OVERALL CONFIDENCE: Medium

**Reason:** Strong signal that variable reward rates cause user confusion across multiple digital-first cards, but limited evidence of competitors building sophisticated post-transaction explanation features. The 800 monthly support tickets suggest real pain, but no direct user research found in sources to validate specific solution approaches.

---

## SUMMARY:

- Digital-first cards show rates but don't explain earning logic causing continued user confusion
- Slice eliminated confusion with flat rates while OneCard still faces support questions despite transparency
- Medium confidence due to limited evidence of post-transaction explanation features in market

# CS IMPACT ANALYSIS: Rewards Earning Rules Display

## CONTACT DRIVERS (maximum 5, highest likelihood only):

**1. User doesn't understand why they got lower cashback than expected**
- Scenario: User spent ₹5,000 on travel expecting 5% cashback but received 2%. They see the earning rules display but don't understand which condition they failed to meet (monthly threshold not reached, merchant category mismatch, or excluded transaction type).
- Likelihood: High
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't specify what information the display shows, how granular the explanation is, or whether it shows real-time eligibility status

**2. Earning rules display shows conflicting information vs. marketing materials**
- Scenario: User saw "5% on travel" in onboarding email but the in-app rules display shows "5% on travel bookings via PIXEL app only" or has different spend thresholds. User contacts CS claiming false advertising.
- Likelihood: High
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't address how rules display syncs with marketing communications or handles rule version changes

**3. User can't find the earning rules display when they need it**
- Scenario: User receives cashback notification, wants to understand why, but can't locate where the earning rules are shown in the app. They contact CS asking "where do I see why I got this cashback?"
- Likelihood: Medium
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't specify placement, navigation path, or whether rules are shown proactively (at transaction time) vs. reactively (user must search)

**4. Rules display shows technical jargon or MCC codes user doesn't understand**
- Scenario: Display says "MCC 4511 eligible for 2%" but user doesn't know what MCC 4511 means or why their airline ticket purchase was categorized differently than expected.
- Likelihood: High
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't specify language simplification requirements, plain-language translations of technical terms, or examples

**5. User wants to know future eligibility before making purchase**
- Scenario: User is about to make ₹15,000 purchase and wants to know "if I buy this now, what cashback will I get?" The rules display shows historical earning logic but not predictive/forward-looking eligibility.
- Likelihood: Medium
- PRD gap: No - PRD doesn't clarify if display is retrospective only or includes prospective earning calculator

---

## COMPETITOR CX BENCHMARK:

**Contact Driver 1: Understanding lower-than-expected cashback**
- How Scapia handles: Scapia shows tiered unlock system with clear monthly spend thresholds (₹20,000 combined spend unlocks airport rewards). Their approach uses progressive disclosure - simple tier status upfront, detailed breakdown on tap.
- Self-serve or agent-assisted: Self-serve with visual progress bars
- What PIXEL should copy/improve: Copy the threshold visibility and progress tracking. Improve by showing transaction-level breakdown (which specific transaction didn't qualify and why) rather than just monthly aggregate.
- Source: https://www.scapia.cards/

**Contact Driver 2: Conflicting information**
- How best competitor handles: Based on Corporate Insight research, leading issuers maintain a single source of truth for reward program information accessible from multiple entry points (transaction history, rewards dashboard, help center) with version timestamps.
- Self-serve or agent-assisted: Self-serve with "last updated" dates and change logs
- What PIXEL should copy/improve: Implement versioned rules display with effective dates. Add "What changed?" explainer when rules are updated. Ensure marketing team pulls from same API as in-app display.
- Source: https://corporateinsight.com/credit-card-reward-redemption-interface-features-and-design/

**Contact Driver 4: Technical jargon confusion**
- How best competitor handles: Industry best practice per Corporate Insight is to provide layered information architecture - customer-friendly category names (e.g., "Airlines & Travel Booking") with technical details available via tooltip/expansion.
- Self-serve or agent-assisted: Self-serve with contextual help
- What PIXEL should copy/improve: Map every MCC code to plain language category. Show merchant name + category together. Add "Why was this categorized as X?" inline help.
- Source: https://corporateinsight.com/credit-card-reward-redemption-interface-features-and-design/

---

## FAQ COVERAGE (maximum 5 only):

**FAQ 1:**
- Question: Why did I only get 2% cashback when the offer said 5% on travel?
- Answer: The 5% travel cashback requires ₹20,000 total monthly spend across all categories to unlock. I can see your current month spend is ₹12,500, so you're earning the base 2% rate. Once you cross ₹20,000 this month, future travel purchases will earn 5%. You can track your progress in the app under Rewards > Earning Rules > Monthly Milestones.
- Escalation needed: No

**FAQ 2:**
- Question: The app shows different cashback rates than what I saw when I signed up, which one is correct?
- Answer: Reward rates can be updated with 30 days notice. The Earning Rules display in your app always shows your current active rates with the effective date at the top. Let me check your account - I can see the rate change took effect on [date] and you were notified via email on [date]. The app display is the current accurate information. Would you like me to resend that notification email?
- Escalation needed: No

**FAQ 3:**
- Question: Where can I see why I earned a specific cashback amount on my last transaction?
- Answer: Tap on any transaction in your transaction history, then tap "Cashback Details" at the bottom. This shows the exact rate applied, which earning rule was used, and if any monthly thresholds affected your rate. You can also see all earning rules anytime under Rewards > How You Earn.
- Escalation needed: No

**FAQ 4:**
- Question: My transaction shows it was categorized as utilities but I bought an airline ticket, why?
- Answer: Merchant category is determined by how the merchant is registered with the card network, not the product purchased. I can see this merchant is registered as a travel aggregator with utility billing services. Unfortunately we cannot manually recategorize transactions. However, I'll flag this merchant for our team to review. For future bookings, purchasing directly from airline websites typically ensures correct travel categorization.
- Escalation needed: Yes (for merchant category review, but not for immediate resolution)

**FAQ 5:**
- Question: How do I know what cashback I'll get before I make a purchase?
- Answer: In the PIXEL app, go to Rewards > Earning Calculator. Enter the merchant category and amount you plan to spend. It will show your expected cashback based on your current monthly spend progress and active offers. This calculator updates in real-time as you make purchases throughout the month.
- Escalation needed: No

---

## AGENT CENTRE REQUIREMENTS:

- **User's current month-to-date spend across all categories** (NOT in PRD)
- **User's current tier/threshold status for all active earning rules** (NOT in PRD)
- **Transaction-level earning breakdown**: date, merchant, amount, MCC code, category assigned, rate applied, rule applied, cashback earned (Partial in PRD - PRD mentions showing rules but not transaction-level agent view)
- **Earning rule version history with effective dates** (NOT in PRD)
- **User's notification history for rule changes** (NOT in PRD)
- **Merchant MCC code and registered category name** (NOT in PRD)
- **List of excluded transaction types per earning rule** (NOT in PRD)
- **Comparison view: expected vs. actual cashback for disputed transactions** (NOT in PRD)
- **Ability to preview what rate user would earn on hypothetical future transaction** (NOT in PRD)
- **Timestamp of when user last viewed earning rules display** (NOT in PRD)
- **A/B test variant if rules display has multiple versions** (NOT in PRD)

---

## ERROR SCREEN AUDIT:

**Error 1: Earning rules display fails to load**
- Error scenario: User taps "Why did I earn this?" but display shows loading spinner indefinitely or "Unable to load earning details"
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show cached/last known rules with banner "Showing last updated rules from [date]. Tap to retry." + "Contact Support" button

**Error 2: Transaction has no earning rule match**
- Error scenario: System cannot determine which earning rule applied to a specific transaction (edge case, data sync issue)
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show "Earning details temporarily unavailable for this transaction. Your cashback has been correctly applied. Contact support if you have questions about this ₹X cashback."

**Error 3: User's spend threshold data is stale/incorrect**
- Error scenario: Display shows "You've spent ₹18,000 this month" but user's actual spend is ₹22,000 due to sync delay, causing confusion about tier eligibility
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Add "as of [timestamp]" to all spend progress indicators + "Refresh" button + banner if data is >2 hours old: "Spend data updates every 2 hours. Last updated: [time]"

**Error 4: Earning rule has expired but still shows as active**
- Error scenario: Limited-time offer ended but display still shows it as available earning rule
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Implement rule expiry checks before display. If expired rule detected, show "This offer ended on [date]. View current offers" with redirect to active rules.

**Error 5: Multiple conflicting rules could apply to same transaction**
- Error scenario: Transaction qualifies for both "5% on travel" and "3% on all online purchases" - display doesn't clarify which took precedence
- Current PRD handling: Not documented
- Recommended next action: Show "Best rate applied: 5% travel rate" with expandable section "Other eligible rates: 3% online (not applied - lower rate)"

---

## ESCALATION PATHS:

**Scenario 1: User disputes merchant category assignment affecting cashback rate**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS → Bank Operations team (for merchant category review with card network)
- Expected resolution time: 7-10 business days for investigation; category changes take 30-45 days if approved by network

**Scenario 2: System bug caused incorrect earning rule application**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS → Zeta ops (if core banking issue) or PIXEL engineering team (if app logic issue)
- Expected resolution time: 24-48 hours for investigation; immediate manual cashback adjustment if bug confirmed; permanent fix in next release cycle

**Scenario 3: User claims they met threshold but system shows they didn't**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS with access to transaction audit logs
- Expected resolution time: 2-4 hours for transaction reconciliation; immediate resolution if data discrepancy found

**Scenario 4: Earning rules display shows information contradicting signed card agreement**
- Who handles it: Tier-2 CS → Legal/Compliance team → Product team
- Expected resolution time: 48 hours for legal review; immediate escalation if regulatory risk identified

**Scenario 5: User requests custom earning rule or exception to published rules**
- Who handles it: Cannot be resolved - policy decision
- Expected resolution time: N/A - Tier-1 should set expectation that earning rules are standardized and cannot be customized per user

---

## TICKET DEFLECTION OPPORTUNITIES:

**Opportunity 1: Proactive earning explanation at transaction time**
- What to build: Push notification immediately after transaction settles showing "You earned ₹50 (2% base rate) on your ₹2,500 purchase at [Merchant]. Spend ₹5,000 more this month to unlock 5% rate on future travel purchases." with deep link to earning rules.
- Estimated ticket reduction: 35% (addresses "why did I earn this?" before user needs to ask)
- Complexity: Medium (requires real-time transaction processing hook + notification system + dynamic content generation)

**Opportunity 2: Interactive earning calculator**
- What to build: Pre-purchase calculator where user inputs merchant category + amount and sees projected cashback based on current month progress. Include "What if?" scenarios: "If you spend ₹X more, you'll unlock Y% rate."
- Estimated ticket reduction: 20% (addresses "what will I earn?" predictive questions)
- Complexity: Medium (requires spend aggregation API + rules engine integration + UI component)

**Opportunity 3: Monthly earning summary with insights**

# SPECIFICATION: REWARDS EARNING RULES DISPLAY

## CURRENT STATE SUMMARY

Currently, customers cannot see why they earned specific cashback rates on transactions. When customers contact support asking why they received 1% instead of 5% cashback, agents manually check transaction details against merchant lists, MCC codes, and monthly caps to explain the earning logic, generating 800+ monthly tickets. All reward calculation logic exists in the backend system but is not exposed to customers in the app.

---

## SCOPE

### IN SCOPE:
- Transaction-level cashback rate display with earning reason
- Accelerated rewards cap tracking and remaining balance visibility
- Exclusion category identification on transactions
- Standard vs accelerated earning rate differentiation
- Monthly cap consumption progress indicator
- Historical transaction earning breakdown view
- Reward reversal reason display for refunded transactions

### OUT OF SCOPE:
- Reward redemption flow modifications — redemption is DIY and working; this PRD addresses earning transparency only
- Changes to reward calculation engine logic — backend earning rules remain unchanged per existing SOP
- Predictive cashback estimates before transaction — requires real-time merchant classification not available pre-authorization
- Gamification or reward earning recommendations — focus is explanatory transparency, not behavioral nudges
- Negative reward balance auto-billing notifications — separate billing cycle feature, not earning display

---

## FUNCTIONAL USE CASES

### Use Case 1: View accelerated cashback earning with cap status
**Actor:** Primary user (PIXEL cardholder)

**Precondition:** User has completed at least one transaction that earned accelerated rewards (e.g., 5% on eligible merchant) and has active accelerated reward categories with monthly caps

**User Story:** As a PIXEL cardholder, I want to see why I earned 5% cashback on my Swiggy transaction and how much accelerated cashback I have remaining this month so that I can maximize my rewards before hitting the cap

**Steps:**
1. User opens PIXEL app and navigates to transaction history
2. User taps on a Swiggy transaction completed 2 days ago
3. System displays transaction detail screen with rewards earning breakdown section
4. User views "Cashback earned: ₹25 (5%)" with label "Accelerated - Food Delivery"
5. User sees progress bar showing "₹450 of ₹500 monthly cap used" with "₹50 remaining"
6. User taps "Why 5%?" info icon
7. System displays bottom sheet explaining: "This merchant qualifies for 5% accelerated cashback under Food Delivery category. Standard rate is 1%. Monthly cap: ₹500 cashback. Resets on 1st of each month."

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given user views transaction earning accelerated rewards, when transaction detail loads, then cashback amount displays with percentage, category label ("Accelerated - [Category Name]"), and distinguishing visual indicator (e.g., gold badge icon)
- Given user has consumed partial accelerated cap, when viewing accelerated transaction, then progress bar shows exact amount used (₹450), total cap (₹500), remaining amount (₹50), and reset date in format "Resets on [DD MMM]"
- Given user taps info icon on accelerated earning, when bottom sheet opens, then explanation includes: merchant qualification reason, standard rate comparison, monthly cap amount, current consumption, and reset schedule
- Given user has multiple accelerated categories, when viewing transaction, then only the applicable category for that specific transaction is displayed with its corresponding cap status
- Given accelerated cap was reached mid-month, when user views subsequent transaction at same merchant type, then system displays "Cashback earned: ₹5 (1%)" with label "Standard - Cap Reached" and message "Food Delivery accelerated cap of ₹500 reached on [DD MMM]. Earning standard rate until [reset date]"

**Failure State AC:**
- Given backend rewards service fails to return earning breakdown, when transaction detail loads, then user sees cashback amount with generic label "Cashback earned: ₹25" and message "Earning details temporarily unavailable. Your cashback is credited correctly." with retry option

**Priority:** P0

---

### Use Case 2: Understand zero cashback on excluded transaction
**Actor:** Primary user (PIXEL cardholder)

**Precondition:** User has completed a transaction on an excluded merchant category (e.g., fuel purchase, wallet load) that earned 0% cashback

**User Story:** As a PIXEL cardholder, I want to understand why my fuel purchase earned no cashback so that I know this is expected behavior and don't contact support

**Steps:**
1. User completes ₹2000 fuel transaction at HP petrol pump
2. User receives transaction notification showing ₹0 cashback
3. User opens app and navigates to this transaction in history
4. System displays transaction detail with rewards section showing "Cashback earned: ₹0"
5. User sees red exclusion badge with label "Excluded Category - Fuel"
6. User taps "Why ₹0?" info icon
7. System displays explanation: "Fuel purchases are excluded from cashback earning as per program terms. Excluded categories: Fuel, Wallet loads, Cash advances, EMI conversions."

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given transaction is on excluded MCC or merchant, when transaction detail loads, then rewards section displays "Cashback earned: ₹0" with red exclusion badge and category name (e.g., "Excluded Category - Fuel")
- Given user views excluded transaction, when info icon is tapped, then explanation lists: specific exclusion reason, complete list of all excluded categories (Fuel, Wallet loads, Cash advances, EMI conversions), and link to full terms
- Given transaction is wallet load to Paytm/PhonePe, when user views detail, then exclusion label reads "Excluded Category - Wallet Load" with explanation "Wallet loading transactions do not earn cashback"
- Given transaction is EMI conversion, when user views detail, then exclusion label reads "Excluded Category - EMI" with explanation "EMI transactions do not earn reward points as per program terms"

**Failure State AC:**
- Given merchant categorization is pending/unclear, when transaction detail loads within 24 hours of transaction, then system displays "Cashback calculation in progress" with estimated completion time "Cashback will be calculated within 24-48 hours of transaction settlement" instead of showing ₹0 prematurely

**Priority:** P0

### Use Case 3: View reward reversal reason after merchant refund
**Actor:** Primary user (PIXEL cardholder)

**Precondition:** User previously earned cashback on a purchase, merchant processed a refund, and system reversed the proportional reward points from user's account

**User Story:** As a PIXEL cardholder, I want to see why my reward balance decreased after a refund so that I understand the reversal is linked to the original transaction and is accurate

**Steps:**
1. User earned ₹50 cashback on ₹1000 Flipkart purchase on 15-Jan
2. Merchant processes full refund on 25-Jan
3. System reverses ₹50 cashback from user's reward balance on 26-Jan
4. User notices reward balance decreased and opens rewards history
5. User sees reversal entry: "-₹50 cashback" dated 26-Jan
6. User taps on reversal entry
7. System displays detail screen showing: "Cashback reversed: -₹50" with linked original transaction "Flipkart - ₹1000 (15-Jan-2025)" and reason "Merchant refund processed on 25-Jan-2025. Proportional cashback reversed."
8. User taps "View original transaction" link
9. System navigates to original Flipkart transaction showing refund status and cashback reversal linkage

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given merchant refund triggers cashback reversal, when user views rewards history, then reversal appears as separate line item with negative amount (-₹50), date of reversal, and label "Cashback Reversed - Refund"
- Given user taps on reversal entry, when detail screen loads, then system displays: reversed amount, original transaction details (merchant name, amount, date), refund processing date, reversal reason ("Merchant refund processed"), and clickable link to original transaction
- Given refund is partial (₹400 of ₹1000), when reversal detail loads, then system shows proportional calculation: "Original cashback: ₹50 on ₹1000. Refund: ₹400. Reversed: ₹20 (proportional to refund amount)"
- Given user navigates to original transaction from reversal link, when transaction detail loads, then rewards section shows updated net cashback: "Cashback earned: ₹50. Reversed: -₹20 (refund). Net: ₹30" with refund date and reversal date
- Given multiple refunds on same transaction, when user views original transaction, then all reversals are listed chronologically with individual amounts and dates

**Failure State AC:**
- Given reversal entry exists but original transaction link is broken (data inconsistency), when user taps "View original transaction", then system displays error message "Original transaction details unavailable. Reversal ID: [REV123456]. Contact support if you need clarification." with copy-to-clipboard option for reversal ID

**Priority:** P1

## NON-FUNCTIONAL USE CASES

### Performance Requirements:
- **Transaction detail load time with rewards breakdown**: Page must render complete rewards earning section within 800ms of user tap on transaction, including cashback amount, category label, and cap status
  - **Acceptance:** Measure p95 load time via instrumentation; 95% of transaction detail views must complete rewards section render in ≤800ms; test with 50 transactions in history

- **Rewards history list scroll performance**: Scrolling through 100+ reward entries (earnings + reversals) must maintain 60fps without frame drops or lag
  - **Acceptance:** Use Android Profiler / iOS Instruments to verify frame rate stays ≥58fps during rapid scroll through 200 reward entries; no ANR or UI thread blocking >16ms

### Security Requirements:
- **Rewards calculation logic obfuscation**: Earning rule details (MCC lists, merchant IDs, exact cap thresholds) displayed to user must not expose exploitable backend logic or allow reverse-engineering of merchant classification
  - **Acceptance:** Security review confirms displayed information is limited to: category names (generic), cap amounts (aggregate), earning rates (percentage only); no MCC codes, merchant IDs, or classification algorithms exposed in API responses or app code

### Accessibility Requirements:
- **Screen reader support for rewards breakdown**: All rewards earning information (cashback amount, category, cap status, exclusion reasons) must be accessible via TalkBack (Android) and VoiceOver (iOS) with logical reading order
  - **Acceptance:** Accessibility audit confirms: cashback amount announced with currency and percentage, category labels read with context ("Accelerated Food Delivery category"), progress bars announce "450 rupees of 500 rupees used, 50 rupees remaining", info icons have descriptive labels ("Learn why you earned 5 percent cashback")

- **Color-blind friendly visual indicators**: Accelerated vs standard vs excluded earning states must be distinguishable without relying solely on color (gold/green/red)
  - **Acceptance:** Design review with color-blindness simulator (Deuteranopia, Protanopia) confirms: accelerated uses gold badge + "Accelerated" text label, standard uses no badge + "Standard" label, excluded uses strikethrough + "Excluded" label; all states identifiable in grayscale

### Reliability Requirements:
- **Graceful degradation when rewards service unavailable**: If backend rewards breakdown API fails, transaction detail must still display basic cashback amount without breaking page load
  - **Acceptance:** Simulate rewards service 500 error; verify transaction detail loads successfully showing "Cashback earned: ₹25" with generic message "Detailed earning breakdown temporarily unavailable" and no app crash; user can still view transaction amount, merchant, date

- **Data consistency between transaction and rewards history**: Cashback amount shown on transaction detail must exactly match corresponding entry in rewards history; reversals must correctly link to original transactions
  - **Acceptance:** Automated test suite validates: for 100 sample transactions, cashback amount on transaction detail equals rewards history entry amount; for 20 refund scenarios, reversal entry links to correct original transaction ID; no orphaned reversals or mismatched amounts

- **Definition:** (Number of users who tap info icon on excluded transaction) / (Number of users with ≥1 excluded transaction) × 100, measured monthly
- **Target:** 50% of users with excluded transactions view explanation (indicates proactive learning vs support contact)
- **Owner:** Product Analytics team

- **Target:** 60% of users with reversals view detail and linked original transaction (indicates self-serve understanding)
